The surrounding Promise executor is synchronous: Jazzer.js's hook on child_process.exec inspects the command string on the call site, before libuv ever spawns a process, so the CommandInjection detector fires on the harness's single call even though execADBCommand's `.catch(err => err)` swallows the eventual exec error.
argument_reasoning: Only one fuzz-controlled argument matters: the single `command` string we pass to execADBCommand. Jazzer.js's CommandInjection detector plants the sentinel 'jaz_zer' into fuzz input via libFuzzer's compare interception / dictionary and flags any exec() whose command string contains that sentinel. Two detector-local wrinkles decide the input shape: (1) execADBCommand always overwrites `cmd[0]` with the (quoted) adb binary path in the no-system-adb branch, so a sentinel the fuzzer places at offset 0 of the input is lost in the final `execCmd` string — we prepend a single space so the fuzzer's bytes land in token index >= 1 and survive the first-token replacement; (2) Node's child_process.exec rejects strings containing a NUL byte with `TypeError: argument 'command' must be a string without null bytes` which bubbles out of execADBCommand (its outer `.catch(err => err)` is on the Promise, not on the synchronous exec call), stopping libFuzzer before the sentinel evolves — we strip NULs with `.replace(/\u0000/g, '')`. We draw the full remaining fuzz entropy as a string via `provider.consumeRemainingAsString()` for maximum detector reach. No type/shape/length validation stands between us and the sink.

lessons: 7B v4 was tagged confirm-gap on this case: it reached execADBCommand (loaded + reached + sink hit) but no crash fired. Two detector-local reasons likely stopped it: (1) it called `execADBCommand(fuzzedString)` directly, so when the fuzzer placed 'jaz_zer' at the start of the input the else-branch's `cmd[0] = "${binFile}"` overwrote exactly those bytes before exec saw them — the sentinel never survived into the final command string, so the detector hook ran against `"/work/target/bin/linux/adb"` and quietly returned; (2) consumeRemainingAsString can return a NUL-containing string, which Node's exec rejects with a TypeError that execADBCommand's outer `.catch(err => err)` does catch but only AFTER the Promise is constructed — the TypeError is actually thrown synchronously inside the Promise executor and bubbles out as an uncaught rejection, which Jazzer logs as 'fuzz target exited' and libFuzzer treats as a non-security exit. Lesson for shell-template sinks with a token-replacement guard: analyze which bytes of your controlled input survive to the exec call, insert a one-character prefix (space here) so the detector sentinel can land in a surviving token, and strip anything (NULs here) that Node refuses to pass through at all.
